chapter: Jelly Roll, Boyman Ham and piano players
title: Meeting Jelly Roll and Boyman Ham around 25s
summary: He met Jelly Roll at 25s, tells of a lady friend's house and Boyman Ham, a blues and boogie pianist who gambled and used dope.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: When did you first meet Morten? Excuse me.
Jelly Roll. When did you first meet Jelly Roll?

I met Jelly Roll around 25. That's where you'd meet all people, 25 to the 8 quarters. And then during that time, I was very familiar around the place. I had a lady friend. See, I'm telling myself, man. Is that right? Yeah, that's right. That's right.
That's right. That's right. Sure. As long as your wife doesn't mind, we don't mind. She won't hear this.

Well, I had a lady that she ran a house. 1519, Aberdee Street. And she had a lot of stalls in there. In fact, they had white and colored stalls. And she had a little girl. So, I had a piano. Well, the fellas around there, me, I wouldn't allow her to play on the piano, you know, because she was jealous, you know. She didn't want me to play around in there, you see. Well, I kept waiting that kind of bit of. The fellas they had around there, oh, they had a lot of them. Boyman Ham, Black Pete, Jelly Roll, a lot of them. You mean they were playing piano and working? Well, they're fellas. They're fellas that used to be around 25, they'd gamble, but they'd play piano in the saloon. They was on the piano. And all of them had a ton on the piano. And when Coopty would come to the house, now, like Jelly Roll, I got in with Jelly Roll, he was a nice boy with me. I used to give a lot of preference to a fella they called Boyman Ham. He's a boogie-woogie player. And the women used to like him. He was one of them dopeheads, you know, used dope. Yeah. But he played the music that led his life, women like. Well, I got in with Jelly Roll. So I'd give him all the procession of the job there. I'd tell her, I'd say, let Boyman play. And he liked it to play Koch and things. Koch and that piano. He was on that all the time.
He was a pretty good player, too.
Yeah, he was a blues player.
Oh, the Koch player, the gambler. He was a good gambler.
Yeah, he was a gambler. He was a good gambler. He was a blues player, though. That's all. But he had a good talent. How do you mean that? He had a good talent.
What do you mean he was only a blues player?
Because that's the style they used to play. He didn't know the rags then, early.
He didn't know all the rags in the first round?
Oh, he didn't. No, he didn't know all the rags, no, not during that time. He didn't know about all them kind of numbers.
